title: Glaux — Build small worlds.
description: A fantasy console for making and running small games. Code, sprites and four channels of sound, on one 320×240 screen.

hero.title: Build small worlds.
hero.lead: Glaux is a fantasy console for making and running small games. Write the code, draw the sprites and press run, all on one 320×240 screen.
hero.note: That is a whole first cartridge. Open source, dual-licensed MIT or Apache-2.0.
hero.caption: Signal Lost, one of the example cartridges in the repository, running at 320×240.

facts.display: An indexed screen. Every pixel is a palette index you choose.
facts.refreshRate: Ticks a second. tick() updates, then draw() paints.
facts.palette: Colors in the master palette, shared out through object palettes.
facts.audio: Sound channels: square, triangle, saw and noise.

features.title: Everything you need is already on the console.
features.lead: There is nothing to install around it. Glaux brings its own editor, its own docs and its own sound chip, so a game is a folder and an idea.
features.editorTitle: An editor that knows your cartridge.
features.editorLead: Edit your scripts without leaving Glaux. Press F5 to run and Esc to pause. Press Enter on the pause screen to return to your cursor and undo history.
items: Completion, hover docs and signature help for the Glaux API.
Find and replace, go to line, go to definition and a list of symbols.
When a run fails, the editor opens on the line that raised the error.
A log panel on F12 while your game keeps running.
features.signature: Draws a block of 8 by 8 object tiles from the object-tile grid.
features.languagesTitle: Write in Luau, or try Rhai.
features.languagesLead: Both languages share the same functions with small differences in spelling. Luau is the main one. Choose when you create a cartridge: new my-game for Luau, or add --lang rhai.
features.experimental: Rhai support is experimental, and its API may still change.

sprites.title: Sprites and palettes
sprites.text: Draw 8×8 tiles, compose them into bigger sprites, flip them, and recolor them through object palettes. Import a PNG sheet and Glaux keeps its colors.

sound.title: Sound from scratch
sound.text: Shape tones and envelopes on four channels. Crisp one-shot effects and pitch sweeps need only a few lines of script.

projects.title: Real projects
projects.text: Split a game across files and load them with require. Read the D-pad and two buttons, or the keyboard, and log what happens while it runs.

create.title: Code, sprites and sound meet in the same place.
create.lead: A cartridge is just a folder. Glaux opens it in a workspace with tabs, so changing a sprite or a line of code never means leaving the console.
create.palette: The sheet and the 256-color master palette, from the Signal Lost cartridge and the system ROM.

games.title: Cartridges you can run today.
games.lead: These come with Glaux’s repository, as examples and as reading material. Open their code and see how they work.
games.description: A knight is trapped in a dungeon arena. Goblins, then masked orcs, then ogres pour in from the edges. Throw axes, dash through the gaps, grab the coins and see how long you last.
games.controls: Arrows move, Z throws, X dashes. Art from 0x72’s DungeonTileset II, released as CC0.

rows.rhai: The same game ported to Rhai, with the same rules, timing and sounds.
rows.sprites: Single tiles, composed blocks and mirrored copies, drawn from a four-color pack.
rows.palettes: A true-color sheet imported with its colors, drawn again through other palettes.

learn.title: Learn by making a first game.
learn.lead: The guides are short and meant to be followed with a keyboard in hand. The same docs live inside the console too: type docs in the shell and they open, even offline.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.text: Create a cartridge, edit its script and run it.

gameLoop.title: The game loop
gameLoop.text: boot, tick and draw, and where your state lives.

api.title: Script API reference
api.text: Every function, with examples in Luau and in Rhai.

learn.stepsTitle: Your first game in four moves

steps.create: Type new my-game in the shell to create a cartridge.
steps.run: Type run and move the owl with the arrow keys.
steps.edit: Pause with Esc, then press Enter to return to the shell. Press Esc again to open the editor and replace the script.
steps.play: Press F5. The square is yours now.

news.title: Latest news
news.text: Glaux is under active development. You can follow its progress in the repository.

get.title: Get Glaux.
get.lead: Glaux is under active development. Prebuilt downloads are not available here yet. You can build the console from source.
get.sourceText: Glaux is a Rust project. With mise and the native build prerequisites installed, these commands start the console.
get.prerequisites: Check the project and build prerequisites
get.browserText: A browser version is not available. For now, Glaux runs on the desktop.
